pages.title: Chunk loading
pages.subtitle: Fair publication, bounded background work, and a gradual loading horizon.

blocks.heading: What changed
blocks.text: Completed terrain payloads release their CPU lanes while awaiting upload, with a bounded queue. Nearby forest pages take priority over newer distant pages. Forest and local vegetation share upload opportunities. Vegetation projection uses more of its existing 1.5 ms slice instead of stopping at a low item count. Coarse background charts wait for the first visible neighbourhood.

Both versions use the same generated site, High terrain detail, Balanced loading, Medium vegetation, a 900 m view, and 1536 x 864 rendering. Times begin after world-file reading and worker preparation; they measure chunk loading, not total startup. The baseline selects the previous scheduling path in the same test harness. MapleLegends and YouTube share the PC; small differences are uncertain.

Long-view regression: at the same 6 km glacial site, empty forest census pages now share a bounded metadata budget without tree uploads. Full loading: 55.79 s before this final refinement, 44.40 s after. This is a separate sparse-region comparison.

blocks.heading: Fog controls
blocks.text: Terrain settings now have Loading fog and a transition-speed slider. The boundary eases outward rather than racing across the nearby ground. Turning the setting off eases toward the ordinary view-distance fog; atmospheric weather fog remains. These controls persist without rebuilding chunks. Coordinate reanchoring preserves the visible horizon.

blocks.heading: Validation and limits
blocks.text: 8,679 focused fog checks passed. Actual renderer tests verify empty spectator mode, no human model, communities, camps or fauna, and a loaded 600 m terrain/forest footprint. A 400 m flight checks continued loading. Initial asset/mesh-upload stalls remain; this is not a 100 FPS floor claim. Terrain geometry, models, vegetation density and source-world data are unchanged.
